title: ci: add govulncheck job
body:
This should mark any known CVEs in the Go packages used by podman. The analysis are performed in a smart manner (no false alarms).

This can be used as a tool to check and report that we're up to date.

One aspect that needs a decision is whether `govulncheck` should be
a dependency of `success`. Currently it is, but I can remove it.

Strictly speaking, it would block _any_ PR from being merged when
the current sources have an outdated dependency with a known
security issue, which is not good.

OTOH maintainers have the power to merge even if CI is red, and
no one will ever look into the non-required CI job which is red.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
NONE
```

comments.body: I agree with @Luap99. Maybe this could be run as a GitHub Actions cron job nightly or weekly, sending reports to us by email. However, I'm not sure how much benefit we'd actually get from it.
Historically, nightly CI failure were followed-upon when keeping CI up was someone’s primary job. Without that, they  very quickly become ignored.
(And I agree that stopping all work on a vulnerability is unreasonable; stopping all work on a “some code is O(N^2)” DOS is outright unwanted.)

> This has way to many false alarms indeed, anything in the standard library must not be flagged to begin with.

This is why we're using the latest Go version in the check itself. I wish there was a flag to disable stdlib warnings though.

> It is not our job to dictate what go version people use to compile.
> 
> Also blocking all PRs is clearly totally non practical and flagging this on any PR to begin with is just the wrong place IMO.

It can be non-blocking. Even if "required" (a "success" dependency), any maintainer can merge a PR anyway. When not a "success" dependency, it just adds a green (or red) mark for people to see.

> Renovate does create dependency updates for known CVEs and we are responsible for merging them, I don't see why we would need another thing to flag them.

I see people file issues to update a dependency because their scanning tools come up with false positives. This (running on `vX.Y*` branches, not just main, if/when backported) can be an answer to those (currently it is not).

> 
> If we think we need another tool to scan it should be setrup as nightly cron that can send us emails for failures but I at least do not see the need unless there is proof renovate is not good enough. cc @podman-container-tools/podman-maintainers

I agree with @mtrmac that such emails tend to be ignored.

----

Closing as I see the consensus is this adds no value.
